newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week 1.43 pct higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week 1.43 pct higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week on Friday 1.43 percent higher, closing the year with an excellent performance compared with 1995, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 444.12 points, up from 437.86 points last Friday.
CFG25 index, which tracks the 25 most liquid stocks, ended the week at an all-time high of 7031.83 points after breaking 7,000 this week, a stockbroker said.

"The Casablanca bourse is closing the year with an excelent performance of nearly 30 percent against a symbolic 4.0 percent in 1995," Younes Benjelloun, analyst at Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.

The performance was largely due to privatisations, including the introduction of privatisation bonds in January and May, and the floatation of leading private credit firm Credor on the bourse in December, Benjelloun said.
"The bourse trading volume exceeded 40 percent to reach 10 billion dirhams ($1.14 billion) this year compared with 1995," he added.
The Moroccan government partly floated on the market Samir oil refinery, steel giant Sonasid and fertiliser firm Fertima.
The market activity was also marked by heavy trading in large capitalisation stocks such as ONA Group and Wafabank, traders said.
Morocco's largest private conglomerate, ONA closed at 510 dirhams against 500 dirhams a week earlier.
ONA has diversified stakes in more than 100 companies and a capitalisation of more than 8.3 billion dirhams.

Wafabank, a liquid stock that recently merged with Spanish Uniban bank, closed at 556 dirhams, from 551 dirhams last Friday. Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest capitalisation, gained five dirhams to close at 690 dirhams, traders said.
Traded volume on the official market was 37.5 million dirhams compared with 19.6 million last Friday.
